geometry.source_ref: https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/context-windows (read 2026-10-12), 'Context window overflow behavior' — 'If the input alone already exceeds the model's context window, the API returns a 400 invalid_request_error ("prompt is too long") on every model.' / 'On Claude 4.5 models and newer, if input tokens plus max_tokens exceeds the context window size, the API accepts the request. If generation then reaches the context window limit, it stops with stop_reason: "model_context_window_exceeded".'

cells.note: VERIFIED AGAINST THE PRIMARY SOURCE 2026-08-13 and RE-READ 2026-10-12 (values unchanged; the page now lists the 1M models in one sentence rather than naming the platforms), replacing the seed spec as source_ref. The doc names Opus 5 explicitly in a list of 1M-window models, and states the 128k output cap as a property of any 1M-window model rather than of this model. NO access-path id minted: the window holds on the Claude API, Bedrock, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry alike, so by mint-on-divergence there is nothing to fork. GEOMETRY IS THE INTERESTING PART AND IT SPLITS. The prompt-only wall is universal: 'if the input alone already exceeds the model's context window, the API returns a 400 invalid_request_error (prompt is too long) ON EVERY MODEL'. What happens to over-window OUTPUT is version-gated AND header-controlled: 4.5+ accepts the request and stops with stop_reason model_context_window_exceeded, earlier models return a validation error, and earlier models can OPT IN to the newer behaviour with the model-context-window-exceeded-2025-08-26 beta header. So a pre-4.5 model's geometry depends on a request header — the second instance of the request-dependence recorded in the design note's section 12, and the first with a named mechanism. shared_truncating is correct for Opus 5 and must not be inherited by an older Claude.

geometry.source_ref: magic-context@5ac4408d:packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/overflow-detection.ts:68 — pattern tagged `combined`, attribution confirmed by MC 2026-08-13 as observed-emitting-the-string only. Re-checked by MC 2026-10-12: the pattern is still tagged `combined` collectively for OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek and vLLM, a parsing assumption never measured against DeepSeek.

cells.note: AN EXPLICIT REFUSAL, minted because a specific wrong inference is available. DeepSeek appears in MC's overflow table under the pattern `maximum context length is (N) tokens`, tagged `combined`. MC confirmed 2026-08-13 that the tag was assigned ONCE for the pattern, reasoned from OpenAI's documented semantics, and inherited by every provider observed emitting that string — so the per-provider evidence establishes that DeepSeek EMITS the text, not that its wall counts combined. Without this cell a future transcriber mining that table would mint `combined` for DeepSeek with an honest-looking source_ref, which is the inference this dataset exists to refuse. Wildcard because the claim is about the provider's wall and nothing model-specific is known.

geometry.source_ref: models.dev via fusiform's live catalog, 2026-10-12: openrouter carries 379 models spanning 61 vendor prefixes (348 across 59 on 2026-08-13); MC confirmed 2026-08-13, and again 2026-10-12, that the wall which fires belongs to whichever upstream served the request

cells.note: NOT AN ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE — a positive, evidenced claim that this KEY cannot hold a single geometry. OpenRouter routes to heterogeneous backends, so the wall that fires belongs to whichever upstream served the request; measuring once yields a value correct for that routing decision and wrong for the next. GRADE IS `measured`, NOT `unknown`: the claim rests on evidence (the catalog shows 379 models spanning 61 vendors' offerings as of 2026-10-12; MC confirmed the routing behaviour), and a grade of unknown would say nobody has established it, which is false. This is the first cell where kind=unknown and grade!=unknown, and the two fields are doing different jobs exactly as designed: the VALUE is unknown, the CLAIM ABOUT WHY is measured. The reason value forbids promoting any measured report into a stated or bracket cell at this key without a routing discriminant — that clause is what makes it load-bearing rather than decorative.

window.advertised.source_ref: https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/context-windows (read 2026-10-12) — 'Other Claude models, including Claude Sonnet 4.5 (deprecated), have a 200k-token context window.'

cells.note: THE CATALOG AND THE PROVIDER DISAGREE, AND THIS IS THE FIRST CELL THAT CONTRADICTS A PUBLISHED NUMBER RATHER THAN FILLING A GAP. models.dev publishes context=1000000 for claude-sonnet-4-5; Anthropic's own documentation names this exact model as an example of the 200k class. THREE INDEPENDENT REASONS TO BELIEVE THE PROVIDER. (1) The doc names the model explicitly, not a family. (2) Anthropic's window and output caps come in fixed pairs throughout their documentation — 1M models get 128k output, 200k models get 64k — and the catalog gives this model 1M context with 64k output, a pairing that appears nowhere in Anthropic's docs and matches the 200k class on the output side. (3) Every other anthropic row in the catalog obeys the pairing exactly, so this is a lone exception rather than a systematic difference in what the catalog measures. A consumer trusting 1M here sends a prompt five times the real ceiling and gets a 400 'prompt is too long' — the wall is prompt-only on every Anthropic model, so there is no truncation to soften it. Only window.advertised is corrected. The 64k output cap is consistent with the 200k class and needs no cell. UPDATE 2026-10-12: models.dev itself changed this row to 200,000 on 2026-10-07 (fusiform's era history), so on a store that has polled since, this correction matches the upstream and serves no override. It still applies on a store seeded from an older bootstrap snapshot until its first poll.

window.advertised.source_ref: https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/context-windows (read 2026-10-12) — 'Other Claude models, including Claude Sonnet 4.5 (deprecated), have a 200k-token context window.'; this is the dated id the claude-sonnet-4-5 alias names

cells.note: THE DATED VARIANT OF THE SAME DEFECT, and arguably the more dangerous row: a consumer pinning a dated model id is doing so FOR REPRODUCIBILITY, which is exactly the caller least likely to re-check a limit. FOUND BY A MECHANICAL TEST RATHER THAN BY READING. The claude-sonnet-4-5 cell was found by reading a documentation passage; this one was found by running the pairing rule that cell's reasoning established (1M context pairs with 128k output, 200k with 64k) across all 13 anthropic rows. Two rows fail, both sonnet-4.5 spellings, both with the same 1M/64k self-contradiction. THE SWEEP ALSO CLEARED A ROW A CONSUMER HAD FLAGGED. BROCA reported claude-opus-5 as carrying a suspect 1M; it passes the pairing test at 1M/128k and Anthropic's doc names it explicitly in the 1M list, so the catalog is right there and the alarm was the inverse error. A test that only convicts is worth less than one that also acquits. UPDATE 2026-10-12: models.dev itself changed this row to 200,000 on 2026-10-07 (fusiform's era history), so on a store that has polled since, this correction matches the upstream and serves no override. It still applies on a store seeded from an older bootstrap snapshot until its first poll.

path.wall_ownership.source_ref: Measured across the live catalog: openrouter serves 379 model ids spanning 61 distinct vendor prefixes (re-counted 2026-10-12; 348 across 59 on 2026-08-14), and routes a request to whichever backend it selects. The wall a request hits therefore belongs to that backend, not to openrouter — which is why window.advertised at this provider carries not_single_valued_at_key rather than a number.

additive_note: The reason value `not_single_valued_at_key` was added 2026-08-13 WITHOUT a schema version bump, deliberately. Bumping would trigger the file-level refusal rule and cost a consumer all 9 cells over one additive value affecting 1. Unbumped, a consumer that does not know the value skips that single cell and merges the other 8 — which is the correct degradation for an addition.
